rationale: I SHOT THE TOWN BEFORE PLANNING IT — a midsummer afternoon (day 6, 16.5 h, cloud 0.08), a midsummer dusk at 20.0 h, an autumn morning, wide and river and mobile — and the river close-up settles a cue I deferred one pass ago. THE WATER HAS NOTHING OF THE TOWN IN IT. The bridge stands over it and is not in it; nor the mill wheel, the moorings, the lamps down both banks, the clock tower, the spire, the far terrace, the willow on the eyot, the punts. I grepped rather than trusting the picture: the river's only reflections are the MOON's disc (one arc, read by disc and reflection so the two agree) and ONE static linear gradient over rows 3–12 called 'the bank's reflection, smeared toward us' — baked into the GROUND CACHE, so it cannot move with the sun and cannot hold a lamp. The state file's own watch note has been saying the same thing as a number since #135: WATER sd/mean 0.151, and every bit of that variance is one ripple hash. So the flattest large surface in the frame is flat in the one way a new hash cannot fix. I deferred this at #139 with a stated reason — b140 was about to change every surface's light and a reflection built against the old light would be re-tuned within two iterations. #140 landed, the light is settled, and the reason has expired; deferring a cue twice on a reason that has expired is exactly the failure this manager exists to prevent. b145 is the bet: 90 minutes, 150–300 lines stated as expected, first in the queue. The vocabulary is already written — a NEGATIVE z in project() is the mirror of a positive one, which is the same solve dialThrow does for a shadow with the sun replaced by the eye — and both failure modes are priced into `avoid`: it must be a LIVE pass like drawSunShade/drawCloudShade rather than cache, and the lamps must register and repaint after applyLight the way BARGE_LAMP and PUNT_LAMPS already do. THE RUNG, and I want this on the record rather than dressed up. This batch is a 2 and I am not going to call it anything else. I looked hard for the 4b, because `developed` has not moved in forty-four iterations and `passages` has never moved at all, and the answer is that THE MAP IS FULL: GW is 138 and the courtyard, cross street, plaza, quay, river and far bank account for all of it, while the wide frame at 1600x950 already runs edge to edge. A spatial climb has to move the FRAME before it can move the MAP, and the mobile shot tonight shows what that costs — 390 px over 138 cells is 2.8 px a cell, so a phone's Wide cannot hold the river and no fit rule can make it. That closes c217 (the quarter button is the answer, and it is one tap) and it is also the standing blocker on rung 4b, which I have written into the watch notes for whoever plans next. The rung history is 4b, 6, 4a, 2, so the two-consecutive rule leaves this pass room; the NEXT pass climbs, and it climbs by moving the frame. The rest of the queue walks the staleness list and breaks the Connect rut: b146 is #140's own finding turned around (the clock tower reaches z 10.2 and the spire higher, and shTop reads eaveM, so the two tallest drawn things in town throw a terrace's shadow — visible, in the domain #140 already opened); b147 is a correctness bug with a seasonal picture attached (plotCrop answers for a whole plot off its FIRST sown cell, so one hardy cabbage may be holding the winter ceiling for five tender neighbours); b148 spends what #144 measured and was forbidden to act on (FAM_CAP is a DEAD constant past 4 — 5 and 7 return byte-identical numbers — so the seam is FAM_RATE and the window). b149 is the one I would rather not need. THE CONTEXT BUDGET HAS NOW OPENED OVER ON TWENTY-FIVE CONSECUTIVE WORKER ITERATIONS and has been 'fixed' by five manager passes, three of them mine. Last pass I cut for headroom instead of compliance and landed at 43.8/46 with 2.2 KB spare; five iterations put it back to 50.2. The pattern is not the file growing, and it is no longer the fix failing either — it is that the fix is a MOP and the cause is that every worker appends and nothing bounds what one iteration may add. So b149 makes the gate binding on the thing it can actually bound: a quota on an iteration's OWN additions, checked where the worker already looks. It carries c227 with it, because a gate that cries wolf on HEAD is a law in this file and probes/punt.mjs has been breaking it since #141. CURATION. LAWS.md rewritten whole for the third pass running: ten claims promoted out of #140–#144 and every one of them MERGED rather than stacked — the shadow target set and the one-path-filled-once rule became trap (f) of the renderer law (it is what b145 and b146 both need), the corridor-not-a-point rule joined trap (c), re-entrancy at the CLAIM and cap-versus-share and which-band-PAYS all folded into the rate-of-zero law, staleness-versus-untruth into the time law, contention-needs-contention and count-the-slots into the FRAMING law, offset-moves-width-stays into the sun's-hour law, and comment-is-a-bug-report into locate-before-you-judge. Paid for by CUTTING seven claims outright: the shared-helper-signature line (generic hygiene, not this town), the mean-over-drawn-membership line (subsumed by measure-a-share-at-the-CHOICE), the rut-versus-mirror control example, the byte-identical-instants line, the lookAt-proves-the-NAMING line, the LIT[]-is-reset-by-its-cache clause, the two-scalars-one-axis example, and the SCREEN-cull margin rule. 12 laws, 11.8 KB, more claims than it started with. INVENTORY, and this is the part that matters more than the laws: 12.1 KB and 60 lines down to 9.6 KB and 50, by MERGING within domains rather than trimming words — the roadway and the kerb are one line, the two punt lines are one line, the two camera lines are one line, the eave model and eaveBand are one line, snow and wet and wind and mist are one weather-scalars line — and the cap in the note is now 6 lines a domain and 250 B a line, which is a shape a worker can hold rather than a total it cannot see. queue.brief: Two gates in this loop are not telling the truth, and both are cheap. FIRST, the memory budget. context-budget.mjs has read OVER on twenty-five consecutive worker opens and has been reset by five manager passes; it is advisory, so a worker reads it, writes 'OVER 50.2 of 46 KB' into its ledger entry, and ships. The total is not something a worker can fix - but what ONE iteration ADDS is. Give the tool a second mode that reports an iteration's own additions against a quota (one ledger entry <= 1.8 KB, at most one inventory line <= 250 B, at most one cue <= 250 B, merging otherwise), prints the offending lines, and is non-zero when they are exceeded, so the worker's log step can hold it. SECOND, c227: probes/punt.mjs reports a stranding for every night rider, because its test is 'a.eyot after eastOpen() closed' and #131's eastOpenFor() legitimately covers that case. It has cried wolf on HEAD since #141. Fix its test or retire it.
queue.successLooksLike: context-budget.mjs --additions exits non-zero on a staged over-quota inventory line and names it, and zero on HEAD. probes/punt.mjs passes on HEAD and can still be shown to FAIL on a build that really strands a night rider.
queue.avoid: Do not change the 46 KB cap or the 12 KB laws cap - changing a cap mid-run is how a loop stops noticing. Do not make the total budget block a worker: it is the manager's number, and a worker cannot fix it inside its own iteration. And do not retire the punt gate without showing the test it replaces can still go red.
